definitions.definition: A broadening formation is a series of higher peaks and lower valleys. If you draw trendlines across the tops and bottoms, the shape looks like a megaphone or a reverse triangle. StockCharts says it shows a volatile disagreement between bulls and bears. Bulkowski describes the broadening top as having an upward price trend leading into it.
identification_rules: Higher peaks and lower valleys form a megaphone shape: the top trendline slopes up and the bottom trendline slopes down.
There should be at least five touches in total: three on one trendline and two or more on the other. Ideally the second touch actually reaches the line rather than just coming close.
Price should cross the pattern from side to side, without wide white spaces where little trading happened.
Bulkowski's broadening top has an upward price trend leading into the pattern.
definitions.confirmation: A breakout happens when price pierces a trendline or moves above or below the height (or end) of the pattern. It can go either way; Bulkowski finds upward breakouts 60% of the time. The price target is the pattern's height (highest peak minus lowest valley), added to the top for an upward breakout or subtracted from the bottom for a downward one. Price pulls back into the pattern more than 60% of the time after a breakout.
definitions.key_quote: A breakout can occur in any direction and happens when the price pierces a trendline or moves above/below the height of the formation.

definitions.definition: A bullish reversal pattern made of two roughly equal troughs in a row with a moderate peak between them. It marks an intermediate- or long-term change from a downtrend.
identification_rules: It needs a significant prior downtrend lasting several months.
The first trough marks the lowest point of the current trend. It is followed by an advance of about 10-20%.
The second trough should be within about 3% of the first. The gap between troughs is usually one to three months, preferably at least four weeks.
Volume and buying pressure should speed up on the advance from the second trough, possibly with gaps.
Bulkowski: the rise between the bottoms should be at least 10%, and the two valleys should bottom near the same price.
definitions.confirmation: The pattern is complete only when price breaks resistance at the highest point between the troughs, ideally with rising volume or a faster climb. Bulkowski requires a close above the peak between the two valleys. Broken resistance can become support. The target is the breakout price plus the distance from the breakout level down to the trough lows.
definitions.key_quote: Breaking resistance from the highest point between the troughs completes the Double Bottom Reversal.

definitions.definition: A bearish reversal pattern made of two roughly equal peaks in a row with a moderate trough between them. It marks at least an intermediate-term change from a bullish to a bearish trend.
identification_rules: It needs a significant prior uptrend lasting several months.
The first peak marks the highest point of the trend. It is followed by a decline of about 10-20%.
The peaks should be about a month apart (Bulkowski says several weeks). They should top out at nearly the same price, usually within 3% of each other.
The drop into the valley between the peaks should be at least 10%.
Volume is usually higher on the left peak than on the right.
definitions.confirmation: The pattern is complete only when support at the lowest point between the peaks breaks, ideally on higher volume. Filters such as a 3% break or a break that holds for three days help weed out false signals. Bulkowski requires a close below the valley. Broken support can become resistance. The target is the breakout price minus the distance from the support break up to the peak.
definitions.key_quote: Breaking support from the lowest point between the peaks completes the Double Top Reversal.

definitions.definition: In the double crossover method, a shorter moving average is paired with a longer one. A golden cross is a bullish crossover where the shorter average crosses above the longer one, for example the 50-day SMA crossing above the 200-day SMA. The opposite, bearish move is called a death cross.
identification_rules: The shorter moving average crosses above the longer moving average.
The 50-day and 200-day SMA pair is considered a medium- to long-term system. A 5-day and 35-day EMA pair is short-term.
MACD turns positive during a golden cross.
definitions.confirmation: Crossovers give fairly late signals and are prone to whipsaws when there is no strong trend. To filter them, traders may require the crossover to last three days or require the gap between the averages to reach a set amount before acting.
definitions.key_quote: A bullish crossover occurs when the shorter moving average crosses above the longer moving average. This is also known as a golden cross.

definitions.definition: A price channel is a continuation pattern bounded by an upper trend line (resistance) and a lower trend line (support). A rising, or bullish, channel slopes upward.
identification_rules: At least two reaction lows are needed to draw the rising main trend line, which acts as support.
A channel line drawn parallel to the main trend line, ideally through two reaction highs, acts as resistance.
The trend stays bullish while prices advance and trade inside the channel.
Semi-log scales may fit the reaction highs and lows better.
definitions.confirmation: The first warning of a trend change is when price falls short of the channel line. A later break below main trend line support signals a trend change. A break above the channel line is bullish and means the advance is speeding up. Some traders buy when price reaches main trend line support.
definitions.key_quote: A price channel is a continuation pattern that slopes up or down and is bound by an upper and lower trend line.

definitions.definition: Support comes from previous reaction lows, where demand tends to appear. Resistance comes from previous reaction highs, where supply tends to appear. The two behave as mirror images, and a broken level can switch roles.
identification_rules: Support is set by previous reaction lows; resistance by previous reaction highs.
Repeated failures or bounces at the same level confirm it.
Because price can briefly overshoot, levels can be treated as zones.
Broken support can become resistance, and broken resistance can become support.
definitions.confirmation: A break of a level means the balance of supply and demand has changed. A resistance breakout means the bulls have the upper hand; a support break means the bears have won. Price often comes back to test the broken level from the other side.
definitions.key_quote: A resistance breakout signals that the bulls (demand) have gained the upper hand, and a support break signals that the bears (supply) have won the battle.

definitions.definition: A downtrend line has a negative slope and connects two or more highs, each lower than the one before. It acts as resistance and shows net supply increasing.
identification_rules: Connect two or more high points, with the second high lower than the first.
At least three points must be connected for the line to count as valid.
The downtrend stays intact while prices remain below the line.
definitions.confirmation: A break above the downtrend line shows net supply is shrinking and a trend change could be close. StockCharts notes that a trend line break is not the same thing as a trend change.
definitions.key_quote: Downtrend lines act as resistance and indicate that net supply (supply less demand) is increasing even as the price declines.

definitions.definition: An uptrend line has a positive slope and connects two or more lows, each higher than the one before. It acts as support and shows net demand increasing.
identification_rules: Connect two or more low points, with the second low higher than the first.
At least three points must be connected for the line to count as valid.
The uptrend stays solid and intact while prices remain above the line.
definitions.confirmation: A break below the uptrend line shows net demand has weakened and a trend change could be close.
definitions.key_quote: Uptrend lines act as support and indicate that net demand (demand less supply) is increasing even as the price rises.
